summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 20%), COPD, type 1 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and crack-related lung disease was admitted for worsening shortness of breath after recent crack cocaine use. He reported increased leg swelling and a brief episode of chest pain that resolved spontaneously. Initial evaluation showed mild hyperkalemia and elevated creatinine, with slightly elevated troponin that trended downward without EKG changes, ruling out acute myocardial infarction. His dyspnea improved with diuresis and bronchodilators, and he maintained stable oxygenation. No acute cardiopulmonary process was seen on imaging, and DVT was ruled out. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue all medications, monitor weight, and follow up with his primary care provider and cardiologist, with emphasis on substance use cessation support.
